notes: Shopify store, direct HTTP access throughout, no WAF. Nav recovered from the same Builder.io CMS feed as the prior Home-Decor pass. Grepped the full nav feed for Clearance/Outlet/Final/Sale/Archive/before-they-go terms. Found the site's genuine clearance concept: 'Archive Sale' (https://www.the-citizenry.com/collections/archive-sale). Its own meta description confirms permanence, not a temporary campaign: "A collection of limited-edition, artisanal designs in their final run are now on sale. Don't miss your chance to bring home the final batch at up to 60% off." - 'final run'/'final batch' is a clear discontinued/end-of-line signal, so this is recorded with no ambiguity flag. The nav also links '/collections/before-they-go' with the same 'Archive Sale' label in some menus - confirmed via curl -D- that this URL 301-redirects to /collections/archive-sale, i.e. it is a pure alias of the same listing, not a second PLP; not emitted as a separate row. GENUINE SUB-STRUCTURE: Archive Sale exposes real room/type facet children in its own nav dropdown (site labels used verbatim): 'New Styles Added', 'Rugs', 'Pillows', 'Furniture', 'Bedding', 'Decor & Accents', at /collections/{just-added,rugs,pillows,furniture,bedding,decor}-before-they-go. Verified genuine (not padding): every child's product-id set is a strict subset of archive-sale's own 59 ids (0 out-of-parent ids in any child, checked via node script comparing full products.json id sets), and the union of all 6 children (54 unique ids) is smaller than the parent (59), consistent with 5 archive-sale products having no room facet plus expected cross-facet overlap (e.g. an item can be both 'New Styles Added' and 'Rugs'). Emitted as parent grouping row (Archive Sale, qty 59, is_group true) followed by its 6 leaf children. QTY METHOD: page's embedded analytics blob for archive-sale reports total_products:50, but this exact figure is also reported verbatim on two unrelated collections (all-best-sellers, all-new-arrivals) - discounted as an unreliable app-level cap. Used exhaustive enumeration of products.json?limit=250&page=N instead (page 1 returned 59 unique ids, <250, exhaustive); the 6 children's blob total_products values (16/21/4/2/14/9) were independently cross-checked via the same exhaustive method and matched exactly, so those are trusted as-is. CONSIDERED AND EXCLUDED (Sale vs Clearance test): 'The Sunset Sale' (/collections/the-sunset-sale, 23 products, exhaustive-checked) and 'The Fresh Foundations Sale' family (/collections/the-fresh-foundations-sale + room facets -rugs 10, -bedding 0, -pillows 0, -accents 30; parent 43) - both surfaced repeatedly in nav banners (e.g. 'Best of Sale: 25% Off Sitewide', 'Sale Extended: up to 20% off', 'Sitewide Sale: Up to 35% off', 'Sale Picks Under $150' - rotating promo copy tied to these same handles across different nav snapshots). Opened both: no clearance/outlet/final/archive/discontinued language anywhere on either page, only a generic percent-off banner ('Up to 65% Off' on Sunset Sale); named after a season/campaign theme with no permanence signal, matching the brief's 'generic temporary promotional sale' exclusion exactly. Not recorded as rows (not even flagged ambiguous) since the evidence for 'generic temporary sale, not clearance' is clear-cut, not a close call. The zero-product the-fresh-foundations-sale-bedding and -pillows facets would have been dropped as zero-qty rows in any case per the zero-product rule.
